gettingstarted.title: Getting started with the map
gettingstarted.markdownText:
## Getting started with the map

If you're new to the map or using spatial data, our Getting Started video quickly covers the basic functionality you'll need to use to add and interrogate data sets.

If you don't have time to watch the video, we suggest exploring the following areas:

1. Search for a location to quickly find an area of interest
2. Use 'Explore map data' to view the catalogue of available data sets and add them to the map
3. Interact with the data layer, including opacity and toggling on and off on the left in your workbench
4. Click on the data on the map to view more detailed data, including the raw data
5. Change your basemap using options in 'Map Settings' to help make some data sets more visible
6. Zoom and change your view, including tilting the view angle using the controls on the right-hand side of the screen

stepbystepguide.title: Step by step guide
stepbystepguide.markdownText:
## Step by step guide

Launch a step by step guide for various popular workflows below:

step1.markdownDescription: The search is at the top of the workbench on the left.
step1.title: Search for a location to find an area of interest

step2.markdownDescription: You can view the catalogue at any time
step2.title: Use "Explore map data" to view data catalogue

step3.title: Search for data or browse catalogue

step4.title: Add data to map by clicking on + sign or "Add to map" button in preview window

step5.title: Interact with data, including opacity and toggling on & off on the left in your workbench

step6.title: Click on data on the map to view more details by triggering Feature Information panel

step7.title: Change your basemap using options in "Map Settings" to improve contrast

step8.title: Zoom and change view using the controls on the right-hand side of the screen

satelliteimagery.title: Adding satellite imagery
satelliteimagery.footnote: Important: Satellite imagery can take a little while to load so please be patient. If images don’t seem to be loading, zoom out a little bit

step1.title: Find the location to view satellite imagery
step1.markdownDescription: - Use the location search or zoom and pan around the map using your mouse or the zoom controls

step2.title: Add the satellite imagery to the map
step2.markdownDescription:
- Open the data catalogue using "Explore map data" button
- Navigate through datasets to select your satellite option: Landsat or Sentinel, and daily or composite images. This can depend on resolution of the image you need (10m or 25m) and whether you want daily, 16 day composite, or annual average images
 - Select "Add to the map" to view the satellite imagery

step3.title: Filter images to find satellite imagery
step3.markdownDescription:
- Filter images by location to quickly find satellite images for that location
 - Satellites circle the globe many times a day. You can expect satellite imagery to be available for one location every two weeks
 - If you haven't already selected your point of interest on the map, zoom in to select one. You will see the filter applied in blue in the Workbench on the left

step4.title: Select a time and date
step4.markdownDescription:
- Use the date picker to select a time and date. Cycle backwards through previous years using the back arrow
 - Choose another date if your imagery is obscured by clouds. You can quickly cycle back and forward using the arrows next to the date picker

comparetimeseries.title: View and compare different points in time
comparetimeseries.footnote: Important: Any time series data can be compared using the Split Screen Mode, not just satellite imagery

step1.title: Add a time series dataset to the map
step1.markdownDescription:
- Satellite imagery is a good example of time series data, with many satellites going back decades
- Find your location of interest and filter available imagery by this location
-See our Adding Satellite Imagery to the Map guide for more

step2.title: Select the time and date
step2.markdownDescription:
- In the workbench on the left, select the time and date which will open the date picker
- Select a year, month and date, or navigate back to other years and even centuries using the back arrow
- Available dates appear in blue

step3.title: Compare different dates at one location
step3.markdownDescription:
- From the 3 dots drop-down menu in the workbench, press 'Compare' to activate Split Screen Mode
- A duplicate copy of your dataset will appear in the workbench
- Choose the dates you want to compare on the left and right of the screen
- Drag the slider using the white button to swipe and compare the two image dates

step4.title: Close Split Screen Mode
step4.markdownDescription:
- Escape the Split Screen Mode by pressing the 'x' of Split Screen Mode title in the workbench
- Remove the duplicate copy of your dataset in the workbench using the 3 dots drop-down menu

helpContentTerm7.content: The dataset you added to your workbench that allows for difference calculations

about.title: About Aeolian
about.htmlContent:
The impetus that energy policies with their ambitious targets for the reduction of green house gas emissions for 2030 and 2050 are giving to the development of the wind sector, combined with the growing attention towards offshore wind, makes it particularly urgent to have accurate and reliable data on the availability and distribution of wind resources in the national territory, both to allow correct territorial planning and as a support tool for the implementation of effective and sustainable interventions.

The goal of AEOLIAN is, therefore, to provide an anemological database on the Italian territory that can be consulted through an easily usable WebGIS tool in order to constitute a tangible support to energy planning for various stakeholders, such as wind farm builders, authorities responsible for territorial planning, companies involved in the development of the electricity grid or even private citizens.

AEOLIAN has been developed to provide information on the general distribution of wind resources in Italy and to help identify areas where these resources may be of interest for energy exploitation. However, it should be noted that the contents of the Atlas cannot and do not intend to replace the detailed evaluation framework (micrositing) that anyone intending to build a wind farm for the production of electricity must always and in any case acquire at the candidate sites in order to address them from an anemological point of view.

All the data presented (even those derived from statistical data) are provided for study and research purposes and do not in any way replace the data produced by the appointed subjects (eg: GSE, ANEV).

RSE takes reasonable care in collecting and presenting the information contained on this site and in verifying its accuracy at the time of preparation. However, RSE assumes no responsibility for any inaccuracy or omission of the information contained on the aforementioned website. RSE is not responsible for the data and news published where processed by third parties and for the content of any other site that can be reached from the site itself or through which this site can be accessed. RSE assumes no responsibility for any decision based on the information contained in the aforementioned website which remains the sole responsibility of the visitor, nor for any loss or damage, direct or indirect, which may arise from the use of the aforementioned website and the information published. The documents contained on the aforementioned website may be subject to change at any time without notice.

Methodology

The new AEOLIAN Italian Wind Atlas provides an updated anemological database consisting of 30 years (1990-2019) of hourly wind data with a horizontal resolution of 1.4 km covering the entire Italian territory and marine areas, estimated through the meteorological model Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) combined with a statistical post-processing based on Analog Ensemble (AnEn). Initially, dynamic simulations were performed at an hourly rate for the period 1990-2019 with a horizontal resolution of 4 km. For the period 2015-2019, a nesting with an internal grid of 1.33 km was subsequently carried out, subsequently using the AnEn to extend the 5-year high-resolution processing back in time to 1990, in order to create a 30-year high-resolution dataset covering all of Italy and the surrounding marine areas. The final resolution of the dataset following the reprojection on this WebGIS is equal to 1.4 km in the WGS84 UTM32 reference system.

These calculations are the result of a collaboration between Ricerca sul Sistema Energetico (RSE) SpA and the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR).

For further information, please refer to the System Research report «Il Nuovo Atlante Eolico Italiano: sviluppo e guida d’uso per l’utente».

The historical data relating to the anemometric stations can currently be consulted by the Integrated Atlas and downloadable from GeoDB ETA.
